verdict.rationale: Pipecat documents an STT latency-tuning guide that defines Time To Final Segment and ships measured P99 latency values per supported STT service, plus built-in metrics. That is real tuning guidance behind its "ultra-low latency" claim, but it covers only the STT/turn-detection stage, not end-to-end voice-to-voice latency. missing for 10: documented end-to-end (user-stops-speaking to bot-audio) latency numbers, published benchmark figures tied to the ultra-low-latency claim, tuning guidance beyond the STT stage (LLM/TTS/transport), independent or hands-on corroboration of measured latency.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can see documented end-to-end voice latency numbers or tuning guidance backing the platform's speed claims

citations.quote: Pipecat ships with measured P99 latency values for each supported service so that turn detection can account for this delay automatically.
Time To Final Segment (TTFS) measures how long it takes from the moment a user stops speaking until the STT service delivers the final transcript.
Pipecat offers built-in metrics for both, which can be enabled with straightforward configuration options.
Orchestrate 150+ AI services with ultra-low latency.
